candidate.answerReason: There are 12 equally likely quarter-sector/third-sector pairs. Three pairs give two odd numbers and two pairs give two even numbers, for probability 5/12.

methods.label: Count equally likely sector pairs
methods.explanation:
Use the usual model of fair wheels spun independently. The first wheel has quarter-circle regions labeled \(1\) and \(2\), and a half-circle region labeled \(3\). The second wheel has three equal regions labeled \(4\), \(5\), and \(6\).

For counting, imagine splitting the first wheel's region labeled \(3\) into two equal quarters. The first wheel now has four equally likely quarter-regions, with labels \(1,2,3,3\). Pairing each quarter-region with each of the second wheel's three regions gives \(4\times3=12\) equally likely outcomes. Counting regions separately keeps both ways of landing on \(3\).

A sum is even exactly when both numbers are odd or both are even. The first wheel has three odd quarter-regions, each of which can pair with the region labeled \(5\), giving \(3\) outcomes. Its one even quarter-region, labeled \(2\), can pair with either \(4\) or \(6\), giving \(2\) outcomes. These cases include every even sum and cannot overlap.

Thus the probability is
\[
\frac{3+2}{12}=\boxed{\frac{5}{12}},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
